walkthroughs.body_html:
A complete warm-up has four parts:

  1. Pulse raiser — jog to lift heart rate.
  2. Mobilisation — move joints through range.
  3. Stretching — dynamic stretches for sport.
  4. Sport-specific — ball work or skill drills.

Benefits include reduced injury risk and better performance.

A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate, removes lactic acid, prevents blood pooling and reduces DOMS (delayed onset muscle soreness). Use light jogging followed by static stretches held 20-30 seconds.
Max HR = 220 − age. A 15-year-old has max HR of 205 bpm. Aerobic zone = 60-80% of max HR. For our 15-year-old: 60% = 123 bpm, 80% = 164 bpm. Training in this zone builds endurance.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Doing less over time.
They are different names for the same component.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
